Role definition · All Divisions · 2026-09-28

Project Manager

Purpose

The Project Manager owns the outcome of every project they are assigned. They are accountable for execution, profitability, customer satisfaction, and completion, and for delivering each project safely, efficiently, and within budget.

Primary responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Protect gross profit at the job level.
  • Ensure job-specific budget adherence.
  • Manage labor efficiency and productivity.
  • Manage material costs and procurement.
  • Identify financial risks and opportunities within projects.
  • Review and approve or reject subcontractor invoices — verify the work performed and the numbers before approving.
  • Confirm the job is within budget before it goes to invoicing.
  • Respond promptly when a revision or change order is needed — invoicing waits on it.

Project Execution

  • Manage day-to-day production activities.
  • Coordinate labor, equipment, and materials.
  • Ensure quality standards are met.
  • Perform job-level quality control and confirm the complete approved Scope of Work was performed before closeout.
  • Maintain project schedules and timelines.
  • Ensure accurate job documentation.

Customer Management

  • The PM owns the work, the PC owns the process. Be the customer's contact for the work itself: progress, findings, scope changes, and problems.
  • Manage first-level customer concerns and complaints.
  • Maintain proactive communication throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Ensure customer expectations are properly managed.

Team Leadership

  • Direct technician activities.
  • Assign technicians to projects and manage the crews built for them. Decide who works and when. The PC books it on the calendar and tells the customer.
  • Coach and develop technicians. Formal corrective action is yours. Training & Technical Quality corrects technicians on the spot and tells you the same day.
  • Hold field teams accountable to company standards.
  • Promote safety, quality, and operational excellence.

Estimating (where applicable — see Division Variations)

  • Estimate and quote jobs directly for divisions where the PM owns estimating.
  • Apply proper markup and protect gross profit within division budget ceilings.
  • Photo-document in CompanyCam and notate the job file in DASH.
  • Coordinate with the PC on authorizations and documentation for self-estimated work.

Collections & Reviews Support

  • Partner with the Project Coordinator to support collections efforts.
  • Support technicians in generating customer reviews. The customer-facing technician owns the ask.
  • Reinforce customer satisfaction and service quality throughout the project.

Division variations

Estimating authority differs by division

  • Maintenance & Plumbing: the PM estimates and quotes their own calls directly.
  • Structure: the PM estimates upsell services beyond the existing insurance scope, and work outside a claim environment. That work usually reaches the PM by referral. All insurance-scope work is estimated by Estimator – Shared Services.
  • Emergency: PMs do not write estimates. All estimating is handled by Estimator – Shared Services.
  • Irvine: estimating is handled by the dedicated Irvine Estimator, not the PM.

Authority

  • Job-level production decisions.
  • Labor allocation and scheduling.
  • Material purchasing within approved guidelines.
  • Vendor coordination.
  • Daily project execution decisions.
  • Technician direction and coaching.
  • Crew composition on their projects.
  • Approval or rejection of subcontractor invoices.
  • Job-level quality acceptance — confirming the approved scope was performed.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Division Manager
Operations
Lead TechniciansAssistant Technicians
Shared Services
Project CoordinatorEstimatingTraining & Development
Success definition

A successful Project Manager consistently delivers profitable projects, develops technicians, maintains customer satisfaction, protects company resources, and executes work safely, efficiently, and in accordance with company standards.

Role definition · Structure Division · 2026-09-28

Junior Project Manager

Purpose

The Junior Project Manager supports the Structure Division's Project Managers in delivering their projects. They carry execution, coordination, and documentation work under PM direction while training toward running projects independently. Job-level decisions and customer communication stay with the PM. The Jr PM assists with both as part of their development.

Primary responsibilities

Project Execution Support

  • Support day-to-day production activities on assigned projects as directed by the PM.
  • Carry out the crew decisions the PM has made. The PM decides who works and when, and the PC books it.
  • Report crew, material, and schedule changes to the PM. Once the PM decides, make sure the PC is told so it can be booked.
  • Coordinate equipment and materials for assigned tasks within the PM's plan.
  • Monitor project schedules and surface slips, blockers, and risks to the PM.
  • Flag quality issues to the PM as soon as they are found. The PM decides the fix.

Documentation

  • Keep assigned jobs documented as directed: photos in CompanyCam and notes in the DASH job file.
  • Support the PC with the documentation and coordination needs of assigned projects.

Customer Communication Support

  • The PM owns the work, the PC owns the process. Assist the PM's customer contact on the work itself: progress, findings, scope changes, and problems.
  • The Jr PM is never the customer's primary contact.
  • Scheduling, paperwork, approvals, and billing belong to the PC. Route customer questions on those to the PC.
  • Sit in on customer interactions and expectation-setting as training.
  • Relay customer information to the PM promptly and accurately.

Development Toward Full PM

  • Shadow the PM on job-level decisions to build decision-making judgment: budgets, labor allocation, vendor coordination.
  • Learn quality control by flagging issues to the PM and hearing the PM's reasoning on each fix.
  • Learn Structure's estimating split. The PM estimates upsells and work outside a claim environment, which usually arrives by referral. Estimator – Shared Services estimates all insurance-scope work.
  • Build proficiency in job-level financial management: gross profit protection and budget adherence.
  • Take on progressively larger scopes of responsibility as the PM and DM assess readiness.

Authority

  • Execution of assigned tasks within the directing PM's guidance.
  • Flagging schedule, quality, safety, and documentation issues to the PM.
  • Job-level decisions, quality acceptance, and primary customer communication remain with the Project Manager. The Jr PM assists with them without owning them.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Division Manager
Day-to-Day Direction
Project Managers
Works With
Project CoordinatorEstimator – Shared ServicesTechnicians
Success definition

A successful Junior Project Manager reliably takes execution load off the PMs they support, and keeps assigned work documented and on schedule. They grow steadily in decision-making and customer-facing skill, and progress toward running projects independently.

Role definition · All Divisions · 2026-09-28

Project Coordinator

Purpose

The Project Coordinator keeps proper movement in the job cycle and collections. They own the administrative and coordination backbone of every job in their division: documentation, authorizations, scheduling, and collections. That work frees Project Managers to focus on execution and gets the division paid on time.

Primary responsibilities

Job Setup & Documentation

  • Take ownership of every file running through the division, from the moment it lands until it is closed or handed on.
  • Own the jobs already open on the desk when you take it over. An inherited file is yours from the day you receive it, whatever its history.
  • Set up and maintain jobs in DASH (CRM/job system) and CompanyCam (photo system).
  • Work the additional systems your division requires alongside those two. See Division Variations.
  • Own documentation integrity — ensure files, photos, and records meet the standards set by Project Coordinator Manager.
  • Verify field documentation is uploaded: moisture readings, photos, and logs. Flag the PM when anything is missing.

Authorizations & Contracts

  • Send and obtain signature on Work Authorizations (emergency work) and Contracts (scheduled work) through PandaDoc.
  • Prep and hand off converted sales files for contract drafting. The estimator converts the lead. The PC runs the paperwork from there.
  • Confirm written approval is in place before work begins: a signed Work Authorization for emergency work, or a signed contract and deposit for contracted work.
  • Manage subcontractor paperwork and addendums before work commences.

Scheduling & Coordination

  • The PM owns the work, the PC owns the process. Be the customer's contact for scheduling, paperwork, approvals, and billing. The PM carries progress, findings, and scope.
  • Maintain the division's calendars.
  • Contact the customer for a warm introduction, and prep them on the next steps of the process.
  • Communicate the crew schedule directly with the customer once the PM sets it.
  • Coordinate scheduling and information flow between office, PM, and field.

Invoicing & Collections

  • Own collections for the division. Drive outstanding balances to paid, and escalate to the PM when one is stuck.
  • Request the invoice from Accounting once the job is billable, and confirm it went out. Accounting issues it through QuickBooks.
  • Coordinate invoicing documentation with Accounting.
  • Monitor the Aging AR list and follow up on unpaid invoices.

Intake & Dispatch

  • Own phone and email intake for the division supported.
  • Transfer misdirected calls and emails to the correct division's PC. Once routed, the receiving division's PC owns the intake and dispatch.
  • Post the dispatch to Slack and confirm a responder has accepted.
  • Keep the caller updated until the responder takes over communication.
  • Where the division runs an on-call rotation, establish it and give it to the Project Coordinator Manager. See Division Variations.

Permits

  • Open the permit process as soon as the estimator identifies a project that requires one.
  • Prepare, submit, and track permit applications through issuance, including online municipal portals.
  • Keep the PM and estimator current on permit status so it can be reflected in the project schedule.
  • Maintain permit documentation in the job file.
  • Permits requiring in-person filing or municipal field coordination are handled by the division role that performs them — the PC still tracks them to issuance.

Client Follow-Up

  • Post-completion follow-up with clients to confirm satisfaction.
  • Support technician review requests as part of post-completion follow-up.

Ownership Transfer

  • Thoroughly review all job communication and documentation before a file is reassigned to the next division.
  • Hand on a file the receiving coordinator can work the day it arrives.
  • Name anything missing before the transfer rather than letting the receiving division discover it.

Division variations

Where jobs come from

  • Emergency and Structure: jobs arrive from the Estimating Coordinator, already converted. Capture the signature through PandaDoc and take the file from there.
  • Structure: work outside a claim environment usually reaches the PM by referral, and the PM estimates it. Once the customer approves, capture the signature through PandaDoc the same way.
  • Maintenance, Plumbing, and Irvine: the PC is the front door. Take the job in, assign the Project Manager, and obtain approval directly, without the Estimating Coordinator.
  • Emergency and Structure: the estimator carries the adjuster. Negotiation, disputed items, supplements, and the carrier follow-up cadence are the estimator's. Support it by flagging gap days rather than duplicating the outreach.
  • Emergency and Structure: the invoice follows carrier agreement. The estimator reports agreement, the PC requests the invoice, and Accounting issues it. Invoicing before agreement puts an uncollectable balance on the Aging AR list.
  • This follows the work type. Only Emergency and Structure run insurance claim environment work.

Emergency intake and on-call

  • Emergency, Plumbing, and Irvine: time-critical emergency intake and dispatch, and an on-call rotation. An active leak or water loss is the standard these divisions work to.
  • Maintenance and Structure: intake and dispatch run the same way, without the time pressure and without an on-call rotation.

Permits

  • Structure and Irvine: routine. Expect a permit on most rebuild work.
  • Maintenance and Plumbing: occasional.
  • Emergency: rare.

Who the division serves

  • Emergency and Structure: carriers, adjusters, and insureds.
  • Maintenance: HOA communities. Some hold monthly recurring maintenance contracts. Others are preferred-vendor relationships that send work orders.
  • Plumbing: HOA community work outside a maintenance contract, plus commercial and residential.
  • Irvine: The Irvine Co. only. The division works to one client's systems and standards.

Systems beyond DASH and CompanyCam

  • Irvine: Coupa.
  • Emergency, Structure, Maintenance, and Plumbing: Avid Exchange, Vendor Cafe, and the CELCO BI tools.

Collections

  • The pursuit standard is the same in every division.
  • Irvine: Irvine Co.'s billing systems set how invoices are submitted and followed. The mechanics differ. The standard does not.

Authority

  • Whether a job has the documentation and signed authorization required to proceed (can flag or hold).
  • Collections outreach for their division, worked to the cadence the Project Coordinator Manager sets.
  • Permit submission and follow-up for the division's projects.
  • Flagging stalled, undocumented, or at-risk jobs.
  • Note: a job leaves a PC's desk through a handoff this role defines, or by the Project Coordinator Manager's decision. The PC does not reassign her own jobs.
  • Note: documentation standards are set by Project Coordinator Manager. The PC owns meeting those standards, not defining them.
  • Note: the PC reports to the Project Coordinator Manager and works for the division. Where a division priority and a company standard collide, the standard holds. Raise it to both managers rather than choosing between them.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Project Coordinator Manager
Day-to-Day Direction
Division Manager
Operations
Project Manager
Shared Services
AccountingSales / Estimating
Success definition

A successful Project Coordinator keeps jobs fully documented and authorized, moving on schedule, and collected on time. The division's paperwork is clean, its receivables are current, and its PMs are free to run the work.

Role definition · Shared Services · 2026-08-23

Sales Manager

Purpose

The Sales Manager owns CELCO's sales function: the estimate-first pipeline that turns leads into profitable work. They lead the Shared Services Estimator team and are accountable for how every lead is worked from receipt to conversion. They set the standard for estimating quality, margin protection, and carrier relationships across the function. The function serves primarily the Emergency and Structure divisions, whose work runs through insurance claims. Maintenance, Plumbing, and Irvine estimate through their own channels per the company estimating map.

Primary responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Manage, develop, and hold accountable the Shared Services Estimator team.
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard estimators.
  • Manage leads and balance workload across the team — the Estimating Coordinator assigns them.
  • Coach estimators on inspection quality, estimate craft, and negotiation.
  • Ride along on an occasional inspection as a quality check and a coaching opportunity. This is a periodic sample, not attendance at every inspection.
  • Spread ride-alongs across the team so every estimator is seen in the field from time to time.
  • Coach onsite while the job is in front of you. Field coaching lands better than a conversation afterward.

Pipeline & Conversion

  • Own the estimate-first pipeline. Every lead has an owner and a next step, and is worked promptly from receipt to conversion or a documented close. Conversion means approval to move forward. No lead dies unworked.
  • Monitor conversion across lead types: carrier referrals, mitigation handoffs, competitive bids, HOA leads, and marketing-funnel leads.
  • Step into escalated negotiations when a contract, adjuster, or client requires manager-level involvement.
  • Take the negotiation whenever it would put a job over budget or cut significant scope. Estimators hold discretion only while the outcome stays budget positive.
  • Partner with the COO on forecasting. The sales function sees what is coming, what is dying, and what is converting.

Estimating Standards & Margin

  • Set the estimating standards the team works to — scope accuracy, estimate quality, and documentation.
  • Keep the function claim-ready — estimates prepared in insurance format for adjuster negotiation, even on leads that never become claims.
  • Own platform discipline across the function: Xactimate estimates and carrier-platform submissions (XactAnalysis, Sedgwick, WestHill) done right and on time.
  • Protect gross margin across the pipeline through estimating best practices, within division budget ceilings.
  • Review estimates before delivery where the loss is over $25,000, the estimate is off budget, or the scope carries complex trades.

Relationships & Alignment

  • Own carrier, adjuster, and referral-source relationship strategy for the sales function.
  • Win and maintain CELCO's placement in carrier preferred-vendor programs — the direct pipeline of carrier referrals.
  • Partner with Marketing on estimate-first lead flow and feedback on which channels produce.
  • Partner with the Emergency and Structure Division Managers to align sales opportunities with operational capacity.
  • Ensure converted leads move cleanly through the PC — Work Authorizations for emergency services, and file handoffs to the Structure division for contract, signature, and deposit.

Authority

  • Lead management and workload across the Shared Services Estimator team.
  • Estimating standards, platform discipline, and margin expectations for the sales function.
  • Escalated pricing and negotiation decisions within division budget ceilings.
  • Approval of any estimate over $25,000, any estimate off budget, and any scope carrying complex trades, before it is delivered.
  • Estimator hiring recommendations and performance management.
  • How often ride-alongs happen, which estimators they cover, and what gets coached.
  • Note: the Irvine Estimator reports through the Irvine Division Manager — Irvine estimating sits outside this line.
  • Note: Maintenance and Plumbing Project Managers estimate their own calls — those divisions sit outside this line.

Key partnerships

Reports To
CEO
Manages
Estimator – Shared Services
Works With
MarketingDivision ManagersProject Coordinators
External
CarriersAdjustersReferral Sources
Success definition

A successful Sales Manager runs a pipeline where every lead is worked and converted at a high rate. Estimators are developed and held to a consistent standard, and margin is protected on every job. Carrier and adjuster relationships earn CELCO the last look. The Emergency and Structure divisions receive clean, executable, profitable jobs at a volume that matches their capacity.

Role definition · Shared Services · 2026-09-28

Estimator – Shared Services

Purpose

The Shared Services Estimator captures and converts leads into profitable work. They serve primarily the Emergency and Structure divisions, whose work runs through insurance claims. They estimate in insurance format to be negotiation-ready with adjusters, and every lead gets that claim-ready approach whether or not it becomes a claim. They own the estimate from inspection to converted lead, protecting CELCO's margin while winning the work. They are CELCO's professional face to insureds, adjusters, carriers, and direct customers.

Primary responsibilities

First Contact & Scheduling

  • Work every lead type assigned: carrier referrals, mitigation handoffs, competitive bids, HOA leads, and marketing-funnel leads.
  • Make first contact with the customer on every assigned lead. Introduce CELCO, gather the detail the intake call could not capture, and agree the inspection date and time.
  • Report the confirmed appointment to the Estimating Coordinator, who places it on the company calendar.
  • Keep the appointment once it is booked, and give notice before moving one.

Inspection & Documentation

  • Build rapport with the customer onsite. The inspection is often their first face-to-face contact with CELCO, and the impression made there carries through the job.
  • Conduct thorough inspections with photos and notes, using the tools each job type requires. Add video walkthroughs as needed.
  • Document every affected room, and determine which additional rooms the scope will consequentially reach.
  • Identify permit and architectural committee review requirements at inspection, and record them so they travel with the file.
  • Photo-document all inspections in CompanyCam and notate the job file in DASH.
  • Host the Sales Manager on occasional ride-along inspections, and put the field coaching into practice on the next job.

Estimate Preparation

  • For claim environment work, write the estimate in Xactimate, claims-ready, so it is negotiation-ready with an adjuster.
  • Xactimate remains the default outside a claim environment. Proposal format is the exception, used only for a strict remodel or capital improvement that cannot become a claim.
  • Write every Xactimate estimate in CELCO format, with trade and activity headers separating the work in each room.
  • Upload and submit to carrier platforms (XactAnalysis, Sedgwick, WestHill) as required.
  • Protect CELCO's gross margin within division budget ceilings on every estimate, in either format.

Conversion & Negotiation

  • Send estimates to all customers, copying all relevant parties: insureds, adjusters, and direct clients.
  • Negotiate scope and pricing with adjusters to secure profitable contracts.
  • Negotiate at your own discretion while the outcome stays budget positive, including minor reductions in scope.
  • Bring the Sales Manager in before agreeing anything that takes the job over budget or cuts significant scope.
  • Build relationships with carriers, adjusters, property managers, and HOAs strong enough to earn CELCO the last look on competitive bids.
  • Maintain consistent relationship touches with adjusters, property managers, and HOA boards that keep CELCO top-of-mind for referrals.

Delivery, Conversion & Supplements

  • Deliver every estimate with its supporting documentation as a single package, not as a bare estimate.
  • Secure approval from the carrier and the customer, and report it to the Estimating Coordinator. Approval moves the file. The receiving division captures the signature.
  • For repairs, send the Xactimate scope and components sheets to the Estimating Coordinator for DASH upload before the file is handed off.
  • Provide the Project Coordinator and Project Manager the approved scope breakdowns they need to execute.
  • Stay in communication with the Project Manager for the life of the job, so supplement opportunities are captured rather than lost.
  • On completed claim work the invoice follows carrier agreement. Report agreement to the Project Coordinator the day it is reached, so she can request the invoice.

Authority

  • The estimate: scope, pricing, and margin protection within division budget ceilings.
  • Scoping decisions during inspection, including which rooms the scope consequentially reaches.
  • Identifying permit and architectural committee review requirements at inspection.
  • Carrier submission and adjuster negotiation strategy.
  • Negotiation decisions that keep the job budget positive, including minor reductions in scope.
  • A negotiation heading over budget or toward a significant scope reduction goes to the Sales Manager before it is agreed.
  • Authority over the estimate ends at the review thresholds. A loss over $25,000, an estimate off budget, or a scope carrying complex trades goes to the Sales Manager first.
  • Escalating to the Sales Manager whenever scope, pricing, or a customer or carrier position needs backing, with or without a review threshold in play.
  • Note: this role serves the Emergency and Structure divisions. Maintenance, Plumbing, and Irvine estimate through their own channels per the company estimating map.

Success definition

A successful Shared Services Estimator works every lead assigned to them, inside and outside a claim environment, converting them into profitable, accurately-scoped work at a high rate. They protect margin, surface supplement opportunities, and maintain the relationships that keep bids and referrals coming. Every converted lead reaches the division that will do the work, prepped and ready.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Irvine Estimator

Purpose

The Irvine Estimator drives estimating exclusively for Irvine Co. The client's community-specific guidelines, client base, and daily on-site geography require a dedicated estimator. They estimate Irvine's work to its standards and support the division's pipeline directly.

Primary responsibilities

Remediation & Rebuild Estimating

  • Write estimates for new remediation projects and for rebuild projects.
  • Estimate Irvine Co. work to its specific guidelines and standards.
  • Travel to Irvine communities daily as the work requires.
  • Photo-document inspections in CompanyCam and notate the job file in DASH.
  • Apply Irvine-specific pricing, scope, and client expectations within Division budget ceilings.
  • Ensure estimates reflect the work actually required to complete the project properly.

Schedules & Change Orders

  • Send a tentative rebuild schedule together with every rebuild estimate — the Project Manager finalizes it with actual phases and dates.
  • Write and submit change orders for both remediation and rebuild work.
  • When the PM confirms a revision is needed, make the change and submit the change order without delay — invoicing waits on it.
  • Ensure approved additional work and scope creep are captured through the appropriate revision or change order.

Permits

  • Identify which rebuild projects require a city permit.
  • Notify the Project Coordinator as soon as a permit is required so the process can start.
  • Account for permit lead time when preparing the rebuild scope and tentative schedule.

Coordination & Client Communication

  • Work closely with the PM and PC for job assignments and scheduling.
  • Meet Irvine Co.'s strict client communication expectations — timely, professional, consistent.
  • Maintain relationships with Irvine communities and property managers.

Preliminary Quality Check

  • While onsite writing the rebuild estimate, perform a preliminary quality check of the completed remediation work.
  • Confirm the approved Scope of Work was performed, and raise incomplete work or concerns before the project moves into rebuild.
  • This check surfaces problems early. It does not clear the job: the Project Manager owns the final remediation inspection and the clearance decision.

Handoff

  • Hand off approved work to both the PM and PC for execution and documentation.

Authority

  • Irvine's estimates — scope and pricing on remediation and rebuild within Irvine's guidelines and Division budget ceilings.
  • Change orders and revisions on Irvine work.
  • Field scoping decisions for Irvine work.
  • Raising remediation work as incomplete before it moves into rebuild.

Key partnerships

Division Manager

Project ManagersRebuild SuperintendentProject Coordinator

Success definition

Keeps Irvine Co.'s estimating fast, accurate, and aligned to its specific guidelines and communication standards — supporting the division's pipeline with the dedicated attention its specialized work requires.

Role definition · Shared Services · 2026-08-23

Project Coordinator Manager

Purpose

The Project Coordinator Manager owns the coordination function across the entire company. They set the standards every Project Coordinator works to, and run the accountability cycle that holds the function to them. They develop the PC team and manage corporate onboarding for every new CELCO employee.

Primary responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Manage, develop, and hold accountable all Project Coordinators across every division.
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard Project Coordinators.
  • Balance PC workload and coverage across divisions.
  • Coach PCs on performance and resolve escalations from the coordination function.
  • Manage the Assistant Project Coordinators. Each is assigned to a division and takes day-to-day direction from the Project Coordinator they support.

PC Administration

  • Approve time off for Project Coordinators, and keep division coverage intact when it is taken.
  • Own PC schedule adherence across divisions.
  • Handle disciplinary action for the PC team, with input from the Division Manager where the issue arose in their division.
  • Carry the administrative load for the coordination team so Division Managers do not have to.

Weekly Accountability Cycle

  • Own the weekly PC accountability review — review performance against company standards, add coaching notes for each PC, and distribute to PCs, their Division Managers, and Leadership.
  • Conduct the manual portions of the review, such as divisional calendar verification.
  • Maintain the archive of completed reviews and coaching records.

Standards & Governance

  • Define the documentation standards that all PCs execute against.
  • Own the coordination workflow standard — how jobs are set up, tracked, and closed across divisions.
  • Own PC-side usage discipline in DASH and CompanyCam, and the job data integrity that depends on it.
  • Verify the PCs are meeting the standard rather than doing the work for them: job notes current, collections pursued, and calendars kept.
  • Hold the line on note quality in DASH. A note that lands on time and says nothing has met the deadline and missed the standard.
  • Ensure process consistency across divisions while allowing for divisional needs.

Corporate Onboarding

  • Own corporate onboarding for every new CELCO employee — how the company operates, its systems, and its expectations.
  • Delivery of onboarding sessions may be delegated to an experienced Project Coordinator. The program, its content, and its consistency remain owned here.
  • Hand off the new employee to their Division Manager for division- and role-specific onboarding.

Collections Execution Oversight

  • Ensure PCs are executing collections follow-up consistently across all divisions.
  • Monitor PC collections activity and drive corrective action where follow-up lags.
  • Partner with Accounting on invoicing, receivables, and job costing support.
  • Collections outcomes and AR performance are owned by Accounting / CFO. This role owns PC-side execution.

Authority

  • Documentation, file, and coordination standards for the whole company.
  • The weekly accountability review — its content, coaching notes, and distribution.
  • PC staffing assignments, workload balancing, and coverage decisions.
  • Reassigning a job from one Project Coordinator to another, outside the handoffs the PC role defines.
  • PC hiring recommendations and performance management.
  • Time off approval, schedule adherence, and disciplinary action for the PC team.
  • The collections follow-up cadence every division works to. The PCs adhere to it rather than setting it.
  • Escalation decisions on stalled or at-risk jobs company-wide.
  • Resolving a collision between a division priority and the coordination standard, together with that Division Manager.

Key partnerships

Reports To
CAO / CFO
Manages

A successful Project Coordinator Manager runs a consistent, high-performing coordination function company-wide. Standards are clear and enforced through a reliable weekly accountability cycle, and documentation is clean across divisions. PCs are developed and supported, and every new employee starts with a solid understanding of how CELCO operates.

Role definition · Shared Services · 2026-08-24

Training & Technical Quality

Purpose

Training & Technical Quality protects CELCO’s standards in the field. They audit how technicians and subcontractors actually work: technical execution, safety, professionalism, and presentation. A gap gets corrected on the spot, with a refresher on the standard. Formal correction stays with the Project Manager, and a gap that repeats across crews becomes training this role builds.

Primary responsibilities

Field Compliance Auditing

  • Audit technician and subcontractor work in the field against CELCO’s technical, safety, and quality standards.
  • Audit brand and professionalism: uniform compliance, tool and equipment care, and vehicle appearance.
  • Report findings to the technician audited, their Division Manager, and Leadership, naming the standard each finding sits against.
  • Hold subcontractors to the technician standard. A failing subcontractor goes to the Project Manager and the Division Manager.
  • Go back and confirm a corrected standard is holding. A report is not a correction.

Correcting What You Find

  • Correct the gap in the moment. Deliver the refresher on the standard while you are both onsite and the work is in front of you.
  • Say something every time. A gap you walk past teaches the crew that the standard is optional.
  • Stop unsafe work. Restart it yourself once a simple hazard is fixed. A major hazard stays stopped until the Project Manager corrects it and releases the work.
  • Tell the Project Manager the same day, so the correction holds after you leave.
  • Formal corrective action belongs to the Project Manager and the Division Manager. This role teaches the standard.
  • Escalate to the Division Manager where a finding repeats, is refused, or sits beyond the Project Manager to resolve.

Training the Patterns

  • Build training where a gap appears across technicians or crews, rather than running a session for one person’s mistake.
  • Deliver a simple pattern correction in the field, with the work and the crew in front of you.
  • Run an office session in a controlled setting where the gap needs depth, practice, or equipment.
  • Develop and maintain the training materials used in both settings.

Reading the Field

  • Name recurring gaps that point at a systemic cause: a missing procedure, a tool, a hiring pattern, or a standard nobody was taught.
  • Identify processes that need a written procedure, and raise them to Leadership.
  • Advise on technical accuracy when a field procedure is written or revised.
  • Give Leadership a reliable read on field quality, including where it is improving.

Focus

Field Auditor

  • Jobsite presence, auditing, and pattern correction delivered where the work happens.

Office Trainer

  • Controlled-environment sessions for gaps that need depth, practice, or equipment.

Authority

  • Audit scope, findings, and how compliance is reported.
  • Correcting a gap in the moment with a refresher on the standard.
  • Whether a gap is a one-off, or a pattern that needs training built for it.
  • Training content, materials, and delivery method.
  • Stopping unsafe work in progress, and restarting it once a simple hazard is fixed.
  • Escalating repeated or unresolved compliance issues to Division Managers and Leadership.
  • Note: formal corrective action belongs to the Project Manager and the Division Manager. This role teaches the standard.
  • Note: new technicians are trained by their division. This role gets involved when an audit finds a gap.
  • Note: Operations owns running the processes. This role verifies field execution and builds field skill.

Success definition

Successful Training & Technical Quality means field work meets CELCO’s standards and crews present the brand professionally. Recurring gaps get closed by training rather than repeating. Subcontractors are held to the technician standard, and Leadership has a reliable read on field quality.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Lead Technician – Irvine

Purpose

The Lead Technician runs mitigation work onsite for the Irvine Division, serving Irvine Co. communities. They execute and direct the hands-on work to IICRC standards, and own quality and documentation at the jobsite. During the job they are CELCO's face to the customer.

Primary responsibilities

Field Execution & Onsite Leadership

  • Run mitigation work onsite to IICRC guidelines: water damage restoration (extraction, drying, containment, monitoring), mold remediation, contents manipulation, temporary roof tarps, and temporary board-ups.
  • Follow proper remediation procedure on every project — floor protection, containment, demolition, cleanliness, and equipment setup.
  • Direct the Assistant Technician's work on the job.
  • Set up, operate, and monitor drying equipment. Track moisture readings to completion.
  • Leave the jobsite clean and properly set up before leaving each day.

Documentation

  • Capture photos, moisture readings, and job notes in CompanyCam daily.
  • Take clear before, during, and after photos — work performed, affected materials, additional findings, containments, equipment setup, and final conditions.
  • Keep the job file notated in DASH.
  • Record materials and consumables used on the job — consumables may no longer be visible to the estimator at inspection, so unrecorded means unbilled.
  • Complete and submit daily time sheets.
  • Ensure the job is documented to standard for the PC and PM.

Customer & Professionalism

  • As the customer-facing lead during the job, represent CELCO professionally onsite: uniform, conduct, vehicle, and tool care.
  • Communicate job status and set expectations with the customer.
  • Own customer review generation — request and secure customer reviews, leveraging the face-to-face relationship built onsite.

Safety

  • Follow IICRC and CELCO safety protocols. Use required PPE.
  • Report hazards and incidents to the PM.

Scope of Work & Additional Findings

  • Read and understand the approved Scope of Work before starting — what is to be removed, which areas are included, and what the recommendations require.
  • Work the conditions onsite, not only the paper — identify affected materials and damage the approved scope did not anticipate.
  • Inside the approved rooms and areas: update the floor plan to document the additional work, and proceed.
  • Beyond the approved rooms and areas: stop and obtain Project Manager approval before performing any additional work.
  • When scope extends, update the floor plan to identify the additional affected areas, explain the work required, and supply supporting photos.
  • Never assume additional work is approved. When clarification is needed, ask the PM.

Authority

  • Onsite execution decisions within job scope and IICRC standards.
  • Directing the Assistant Technician's tasks onsite.
  • Documenting additional findings inside the approved rooms and areas.
  • Flagging scope changes, hazards, or additional damage to the PM.
  • Note: work beyond the approved rooms and areas requires PM approval. The Lead Technician does not authorize it.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Project Manager
Directs Onsite
Assistant Technician
Works With
Project CoordinatorIrvine Estimator
Success definition

A successful Lead Technician completes mitigation work to IICRC standards, safely and on schedule, and documents it thoroughly. They direct the assistant effectively, secure customer reviews, and represent CELCO professionally at the jobsite.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Assistant Technician – Irvine

Purpose

The Assistant Technician supports the Lead Technician in executing the Irvine Division's mitigation work in Irvine Co. communities, learning the trade while helping deliver quality work safely and on schedule.

Primary responsibilities

Field Support

  • Assist the Lead Technician across all mitigation work — water damage restoration, mold remediation, contents manipulation, temporary roof tarps, and temporary board-ups.
  • Perform assigned hands-on tasks to IICRC standards under the Lead's direction.
  • Help load, transport, stage, and maintain equipment.

Documentation Support

  • Assist with photo and reading capture in CompanyCam as directed.
  • Handle the DASH job notes when working a job with no Lead Technician present.
  • Complete and submit daily time sheets.

Professionalism & Safety

  • Represent CELCO professionally onsite — uniform, conduct, vehicle, and tool care.
  • Request customer reviews when working a job with no Lead Technician present. The customer-facing technician onsite owns the ask.
  • Follow IICRC and CELCO safety protocols. Use required PPE.
  • Report hazards to the Lead Technician.

Authority

  • Execution of assigned tasks within the Lead's direction.
  • Flagging safety concerns to the Lead.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Division Manager – Irvine

Purpose

The Division Manager owns the Irvine Division as a profit center: a dedicated Irvine Co. operation running its own estimating, warehouse, and rebuild capability across four regions. They set its strategic direction and are accountable for its health, profitability, growth, and staffing. They hold the Project Managers accountable for their regions, and they are accountable for the division's long-term success and its standing with the client.

Primary responsibilities

Financial Leadership

  • Protect division gross profit (blended GP across all approved subdivisions).
  • Achieve division revenue goals.
  • Ensure division budget adherence.
  • Partner with the COO on forecasting and resource planning.
  • Monitor divisional financial performance and implement corrective actions when necessary.
  • Require corrective action on over-budget jobs and timely change orders for added scope.
  • Monitor unbilled work and clear the documentation or approval barriers holding up invoicing.

Growth & Strategy

  • Drive sustainable revenue growth.
  • Develop division-specific growth initiatives.
  • Partner with Marketing on strategic campaigns and business development efforts.
  • Partner with Sales to ensure alignment between sales opportunities and operational capacity.

People Leadership

  • Own division staffing and workforce planning.
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard division personnel.
  • Receive each new employee from corporate onboarding, and deliver the division- and role-specific onboarding they need to start work.
  • Direct the division Project Coordinator's day-to-day work and priorities. The PC reports to the Project Coordinator Manager, who owns their standards, coaching, and performance.
  • Develop, coach, and hold Project Managers accountable.
  • Build succession plans and future leaders within the division.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, performance, and continuous improvement.

Operational Leadership

  • Ensure divisional compliance with company standards, SOPs, and expectations.
  • Partner with Training & Technical Quality to improve performance and customer outcomes.
  • Ensure resources are available to support divisional goals.
  • Confirm Project Managers visit their jobsites — projects are not managed from the office.

Quality Leadership

  • Set the division's quality standards for every phase of work.
  • Require Project Managers and Lead Technicians to complete their assigned quality inspections.
  • Personally inspect projects that are high-value, high-risk, delayed, have failed an inspection, or are drawing complaints. The Project Manager inspects every job. The Division Manager inspects the ones that warrant a second look.
  • Drive down failed inspections, incomplete work, callbacks, return trips, and preventable customer complaints.

Regional Structure

  • Operate the division across its four Orange County regions, each assigned to a Project Manager.
  • Confirm every new job is assigned to the correct Project Manager and region.
  • Balance workload across regions and redistribute assignments when service or schedule is at risk.
  • Build Project Manager coverage as the division grows toward a Project Manager for every region.

Rebuild Oversight

  • Confirm completed remediation moves into rebuild without stalling — approved scope, budget, photos, and clearance in hand.
  • Hold the Rebuild Superintendent accountable for rebuild progress, vendor coverage, and rebuild quality.
  • Review upcoming rebuild starts and subcontractor coverage.
  • Confirm the Project Manager stays accountable for the project through rebuild. The Superintendent supports the work without taking it over.

Visibility & Accountability

  • Know what new work has come in and who owns each job.
  • Know what is pending scheduling, scheduled but not started, and currently in progress.
  • Know what is delayed, why it is delayed, and who owns the corrective action.
  • Know what is pending clearance or ready to move into the next phase.
  • Know what is over budget, awaiting a change order, or trending toward a loss.
  • Know what is complete, what is missing documentation, and what is ready for billing.
  • Know which customers require immediate attention.
  • Confirm every member of the division is completing their assigned responsibilities.
  • Own the division's master tracking spreadsheet: the at-a-glance view of every job and its current stage. Project Managers maintain their regional views. The master belongs to the Division Manager.

Customer Leadership

  • Manage escalated customer complaints.
  • Protect and strengthen the division's reputation.
  • Ensure exceptional customer experiences and outcomes.

The Client Relationship

  • Maintain the relationship with Irvine Co. management and community teams across every region.
  • Take personal ownership of escalated client concerns and drive them to resolution.
  • Conduct periodic client visits and relationship meetings in all four regions.
  • Support the Project Managers in growing CELCO's service footprint across existing and new communities.
  • Protect CELCO's standing as a dependable Irvine Co. service partner — the division's future depends on it.

Authority

  • Division staffing recommendations.
  • Hiring recommendations.
  • Performance management.
  • Division-level resource allocation.
  • Revenue and growth planning.
  • Escalated customer resolutions.
  • Operational decisions affecting divisional performance.
  • Management review of any project in the division.
  • Requiring corrective action on over-budget or at-risk jobs.
  • Assignment of jobs to regions and Project Managers.
  • Escalated client resolution with Irvine Co.

Key partnerships

Executive Leadership
COOCSO
Operations
Project ManagersRebuild SuperintendentIrvine EstimatorProject Coordinators
External

Success definition

A successful Division Manager creates visibility, assigns ownership, enforces accountability, and protects profitability. Irvine Co. receives consistent quality and communication across every region. The division grows, its people develop, and the client relationship it is built on is protected.

Division Manager – Structure

Purpose

The Division Manager owns the Structure Division as a profit center. Its repair work is delivered through subcontractors, on insurance claims and on referral work. The Division Manager sets the division's direction and is accountable for its health, profitability, growth, and staffing over the long term.

Primary responsibilities

Financial Leadership

  • Protect division gross profit (blended GP across all approved subdivisions).
  • Achieve division revenue goals.
  • Ensure division budget adherence.
  • Partner with the COO on forecasting and resource planning.
  • Monitor divisional financial performance and implement corrective actions when necessary.
  • Require corrective action on over-budget jobs and timely change orders for added scope.
  • Monitor unbilled work and clear the documentation or approval barriers holding up invoicing.

Growth & Strategy

  • Drive sustainable revenue growth.
  • Develop division-specific growth initiatives.
  • Partner with Marketing on strategic campaigns and business development efforts.
  • Partner with Sales to ensure alignment between sales opportunities and operational capacity.

People Leadership

  • Own division staffing and workforce planning.
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard division personnel.
  • Receive each new employee from corporate onboarding, and deliver the division- and role-specific onboarding they need to start work.
  • Direct the division Project Coordinator's day-to-day work and priorities. The PC reports to the Project Coordinator Manager, who owns their standards, coaching, and performance.
  • Develop, coach, and hold Project Managers accountable.
  • Build succession plans and future leaders within the division.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, performance, and continuous improvement.
  • The Junior Project Manager reports to you and takes day-to-day direction from the Project Managers. Judge their readiness for more responsibility together with the Project Managers.

Operational Leadership

  • Ensure divisional compliance with company standards, SOPs, and expectations.
  • Partner with Training & Technical Quality to improve performance and customer outcomes.
  • Ensure resources are available to support divisional goals.
  • Confirm Project Managers visit their jobsites — projects are not managed from the office.
  • Permits are routine in this division. Confirm permit needs are identified early and that the PC tracks each one through issuance.

Quality Leadership

  • Set the division's quality standards for every phase of work.
  • Personally inspect projects that are high-value, high-risk, delayed, have failed an inspection, or are drawing complaints. The Project Manager inspects every job. The Division Manager inspects the ones that warrant a second look.
  • Drive down failed inspections, incomplete work, callbacks, return trips, and preventable customer complaints.
  • Require Project Managers to inspect subcontractor work at each phase and before closeout.

Subcontractor Oversight

  • Project Managers select, schedule, and manage the subcontractors on their jobs. Hold each Project Manager accountable for the subcontractors they use.
  • Hold every subcontractor to CELCO's quality, schedule, safety, and documentation standards through the Project Managers.
  • Review subcontractor performance across the division: callbacks, delays, failed inspections, and cost overruns.
  • Direct a Project Manager to replace a subcontractor who repeatedly misses the standard.

Where the Work Comes From

  • Claim work arrives from the Estimating Coordinator, already converted. Estimator – Shared Services estimates it and carries the adjuster.
  • Work outside a claim environment usually reaches a Project Manager by referral. The PM estimates it and sends it without division review.
  • Watch gross profit on PM-estimated work after the fact. Correct a Project Manager whose estimates erode margin.
  • Keep division capacity in line with both sources of work. Tell the Sales Manager early when claim volume will outrun the division's Project Managers or subcontractors.

Visibility & Accountability

  • Know what new work has come in and who owns each job.
  • Know what is pending scheduling, scheduled but not started, and currently in progress.
  • Know what is delayed, why it is delayed, and who owns the corrective action.
  • Know what is pending clearance or ready to move into the next phase.
  • Know what is over budget, awaiting a change order, or trending toward a loss.
  • Know what is complete, what is missing documentation, and what is ready for billing.
  • Know which customers require immediate attention.
  • Confirm every member of the division is completing their assigned responsibilities.
  • Know which subcontractors are on which jobs, and which are behind.
  • Know which claim jobs are waiting on carrier agreement. The estimator owns the follow-up, and the invoice follows agreement.

Customer Leadership

  • Manage escalated customer complaints.
  • Protect and strengthen the division's reputation.
  • Ensure exceptional customer experiences and outcomes.

Authority

  • Division staffing recommendations.
  • Hiring recommendations.
  • Performance management.
  • Division-level resource allocation.
  • Revenue and growth planning.
  • Escalated customer resolutions.
  • Operational decisions affecting divisional performance.
  • Management review of any project in the division.
  • Requiring corrective action on over-budget or at-risk jobs.
  • Directing a Project Manager to replace an underperforming subcontractor.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Project Manager – Irvine

Purpose

The Project Manager owns their assigned Irvine Co. projects from assignment through invoicing — remediation, clearance, rebuild, and closeout. There is no handoff at clearance: the same Project Manager carries the project, the budget, and the client relationship the whole way.

Primary responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Protect gross profit at the job level.
  • Ensure job-specific budget adherence.
  • Manage labor efficiency and productivity.
  • Manage material costs and procurement.
  • Identify financial risks and opportunities within projects.
  • Review and approve or reject subcontractor invoices — verify the work performed and the numbers before approving.
  • Confirm the job is within budget before it goes to invoicing.
  • Respond promptly when a revision or change order is needed — invoicing waits on it.

Project Execution

  • Manage day-to-day production activities.
  • Coordinate labor, equipment, and materials.
  • Ensure quality standards are met.
  • Perform job-level quality control and confirm the complete approved Scope of Work was performed before closeout.
  • Maintain project schedules and timelines.
  • Ensure accurate job documentation.

Customer Management

  • The PM owns the work, the PC owns the process. Be the customer's contact for the work itself: progress, findings, scope changes, and problems.
  • Manage first-level customer concerns and complaints.
  • Maintain proactive communication throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Ensure customer expectations are properly managed.
  • Send the client a daily update on every active project — including days when no onsite work is performed.
  • Own client communication through every phase, remediation and rebuild alike.

Team Leadership

  • Direct technician activities.
  • Assign technicians to projects and manage the crews built for them. Decide who works and when. The PC books it on the calendar and tells the customer.
  • Coach and develop technicians. Formal corrective action is yours. Training & Technical Quality corrects technicians on the spot and tells you the same day.
  • Hold field teams accountable to company standards.
  • Promote safety, quality, and operational excellence.
  • Lead Technicians report to you on job status, concerns, additional findings, delays, and questions.

Regional Ownership

  • Own every project in your assigned regions from assignment through invoicing.
  • Know the status, schedule, cost, quality, communication, and next step for each one.
  • Keep your regional view of the division tracking spreadsheet current daily — including jobs in the drying phase.
  • Publish your schedule daily so the division knows where you will be — inspections, quality visits, and project activity.

Rebuild

  • Finalize the rebuild calendar with actual phases and dates once clearance is achieved and work is ready to begin.
  • Work with the Rebuild Superintendent on vendor and in-house technician assignment.
  • Carry the Superintendent's daily field reporting into your client updates throughout the rebuild.
  • Remain accountable for the rebuild outcome. The Superintendent performs the rebuild inspections. Passing the client's inspection is still yours.

Collections & Reviews Support

  • Partner with the Project Coordinator to support collections efforts.
  • Support technicians in generating customer reviews. The customer-facing technician owns the ask.
  • Reinforce customer satisfaction and service quality throughout the project.

Quality Control & Clearance

  • Perform the final remediation quality inspection once the technician confirms the job is dry and final cleaning is complete.
  • Confirm the complete approved Scope of Work was performed before the project moves toward clearance.
  • Inspect every project personally. Irvine Co. requires an inspection on every job, so the division cannot rely on sampling.
  • The Irvine Estimator's preliminary check during the rebuild estimate surfaces problems early. Clearing the job is yours.
  • Send the post-evaluation request once the project is ready.

Authority

  • Job-level production decisions.
  • Labor allocation and scheduling.
  • Material purchasing within approved guidelines.
  • Vendor coordination.
  • Daily project execution decisions.
  • Technician direction and coaching.
  • Crew composition on their projects.
  • Approval or rejection of subcontractor invoices.
  • Job-level quality acceptance — confirming the approved scope was performed.
  • Final remediation quality acceptance and clearance on their projects.
  • Approval of additional work beyond the approved rooms and areas.

Success definition

A successful Project Manager delivers profitable Irvine Co. projects that pass inspection the first time — regions fully visible, clients updated daily, budgets protected, technicians developed, and every project carried personally from assignment through invoicing.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Rebuild Superintendent

Purpose

The Rebuild Superintendent runs the rebuild phase in the field. They keep vendors, in-house technicians, materials, and inspections moving. Rebuild work gets built to the approved scope, on the approved calendar, and to a standard that passes client inspection the first time. The Project Manager owns the project. The Superintendent owns the field.

Primary responsibilities

Field Operations

  • Oversee day-to-day field operations on every rebuild project in the division.
  • Support subcontractors and in-house technicians with whatever keeps the work moving.
  • Address field concerns, delays, material needs, and site issues before they reach the schedule.
  • Help ensure rebuild projects progress according to the approved calendar.

Quality Control

  • Inspect rebuild work in progress — not only once it is finished.
  • Confirm the work performed follows the approved Scope of Work and meets CELCO's quality standard.
  • Identify incomplete work and defects, and communicate them to the vendor or technician and to the assigned PM.
  • Perform the final rebuild inspection once the work is complete.
  • Catch and correct problems before the client's inspection. The goal is no failed inspections and no return trips.

Materials & the Staging Hub

  • Keep the division's staging hub stocked and orderly — crews start and end their days there, loading and unloading their trucks.
  • Track the materials, supplies, and equipment held at the hub against what current and upcoming projects will require.
  • Tell the company warehouse team what the division needs and when — purchasing and vendor ordering stay with them.
  • Coordinate transfers from the main warehouse and deliveries out to jobsites.
  • Track equipment condition and maintenance needs — equipment that fails on a jobsite costs a day.
  • Ensure vendors and technicians have what they need before they need it — material gaps are avoidable delays.

Permits & Inspections

  • Handle permits that require in-person filing or field coordination with the municipality.
  • Coordinate the scheduling of required city inspections and attend them where the jurisdiction requires it.
  • Keep the Project Coordinator current so permit status stays tracked in the job file.

Reporting to the Project Manager

  • Give the assigned PM a daily update on the progress and status of each active rebuild.
  • Report delays, concerns, and timeline changes the moment they are identified, so the PM's client update is accurate.
  • Raise concerns as they arise rather than at project completion.
  • Client communication runs through the PM — field information flows to the PM, who carries it to the client.

Documentation

  • Ensure rebuild work is photo-documented — progress, work completed, concerns identified, and final completion.
  • Photos must clearly show the state of the work, not merely that someone was onsite.

Authority

  • Day-to-day field direction of rebuild vendors and in-house technicians.
  • Accepting or rejecting rebuild workmanship against the approved Scope of Work.
  • Stopping rebuild work that falls short of the approved scope or quality standard.
  • Requesting materials and scheduling deliveries within approved project budgets.
  • Stock levels and equipment held at the division staging hub.
  • Note: project-level decisions, budget changes, scope changes, and client communication remain with the Project Manager.
  • Note: purchasing and vendor ordering remain with the company warehouse function, and vehicles and fleet remain a company function. The staging hub exists to keep crews off the road to the main warehouse. It does not replace the warehouse.

Success definition

A successful Rebuild Superintendent keeps rebuild projects moving on the approved calendar, with the materials and support the field needs. They catch quality problems while those are still cheap to fix. They hand the Project Manager a project that passes client inspection the first time.

Role definition · Shared Services · 2026-08-23

Estimating Coordinator

Purpose

The Estimating Coordinator runs the front of the pipeline. They take in every estimating lead, set it up, and put an estimator on it. They keep the estimate moving to the customer or adjuster, and hand each converted file to the division that will do the work. The job leaves this role at conversion. Ownership transfers with the file.

Primary responsibilities

Job Setup & Documentation

  • Take ownership of every file running through the division, from the moment it lands until it is closed or handed on.
  • Own the jobs already open on the desk when you take it over. An inherited file is yours from the day you receive it, whatever its history.
  • Set up and maintain jobs in DASH (CRM/job system) and CompanyCam (photo system).
  • Own documentation integrity — ensure files, photos, and records meet the standards set by Project Coordinator Manager.
  • Open the job in DASH and CompanyCam as soon as the lead is captured — before an estimator is assigned.

Lead Intake

  • Take in estimating leads — direct calls and emails from prospective customers, and internal referrals into the estimating department.
  • A lead is ready to assign once it carries all of this: full name, phone, email, address, referral source, insurance carrier and claim details or a clear non-insurance flag, responsible billing party, and a brief job description.
  • Establish at intake whether the call is an emergency, so it can be routed immediately instead of queued.
  • Chase whoever took the call for anything missing — an incomplete intake becomes a delayed estimate.

Estimator Assignment & Scheduling

  • Assign an estimator to each lead based on current workload and proximity to the property.
  • Place the estimator on the company calendar once they have confirmed the appointment.
  • Keep the estimating calendar current so the team’s coverage is visible.
  • Rebalance assignments when a lead is sitting or an estimator is over capacity.

Consulting Jobs (CST)

  • Coordinate CELCO’s consulting jobs end to end. These stay with this role and are never handed to a division.
  • Request invoicing to the hiring party once the consulting work is complete.
  • Own collections on consulting invoices — drive outstanding balances to paid and follow up until they are.
  • Keep consulting job files documented to the same standard as any other job.

Estimate Follow-Through

  • Follow up with estimators after every inspection to confirm the estimate is written and sent.
  • Confirm estimates reach the customer or the adjuster — an estimate written but not sent has not been delivered.
  • Keep the Sales Manager visible on leads that are stalling.

Conversion & Handoff

  • Record the approval the estimator reports: who approved, when, and in what form. Verbal or email approval from the carrier and the customer moves the file.
  • Formal signature is captured by the receiving division, not here. Approval moves the file. The signed Work Authorization or contract gates production.
  • Emergency work converted: prep the file and reassign it to the Emergency Project Coordinator, who captures the Work Authorization signature through PandaDoc.
  • Emergency work requiring immediate dispatch: send it straight to the Emergency Division so its Project Coordinator can prepare the division to dispatch. Do not hold it in the estimating queue.
  • Structure repairs converted: prep the file and reassign it to the Structure Project Coordinator, who captures the contract signature through PandaDoc.
  • Repairs: upload the Xactimate scope and components sheets the estimator sends you into DASH before the file is handed off.
  • Once a file is reassigned it belongs to the receiving division. This role does not carry it forward.

Authority

  • Estimator assignment across the estimating team, based on workload and proximity.
  • Whether a lead carries the intake detail required to be assigned — can hold it until it does.
  • Calendar placement for estimating appointments.
  • Whether a reported approval is complete enough to move the file, and holding it until it is.
  • Collections follow-up and outreach on consulting invoices.
  • Note: the job file leaves this role at conversion. The receiving division’s Project Coordinator owns it from that point. Consulting jobs are the exception and stay here.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Sales Manager
Works With
Estimator – Shared ServicesProject Coordinator ManagerDivision Project Coordinators
Client-Facing
Prospective CustomersAdjusters
Success definition

A successful Estimating Coordinator keeps the front of the pipeline moving: every lead captured completely, assigned quickly, inspected on schedule, and its estimate delivered. They hand each converted file to the right division clean enough to work the day it arrives. They carry the consulting book from intake through to collected.

Role definition · Irvine Division · 2026-08-23

Assistant Project Coordinator

Purpose

The Assistant Project Coordinator supports the Project Coordinators in keeping jobs documented, authorized, and moving. They carry coordination and documentation work under PC direction, so the PCs can stay ahead of the division's authorizations, scheduling, and collections. Documentation integrity, authorization decisions, and collections strategy stay with the PCs. The Assistant PC assists with all three.

Primary responsibilities

Documentation Support

  • Set up and maintain job records in DASH and CompanyCam as directed.
  • Chase missing field documentation and flag gaps to the PC: photos, moisture readings, logs.
  • Keep job files current so the PCs can work from accurate records.
  • Learn CELCO's documentation standards by applying them daily.

Authorizations & Paperwork Support

  • Prepare Work Authorizations, contracts, and subcontractor paperwork for the PC to send.
  • Track which jobs are missing signatures or approvals and surface them to the PC.
  • File executed paperwork to standard.
  • Confirming approval is in place before work begins remains the PC's call, not the Assistant's.

Scheduling & Coordination Support

  • Help maintain the division's calendars.
  • Relay information between office, PM, and field as directed by the PC.
  • Prepare routine correspondence and follow-ups for PC review.

Collections & Follow-Up Support

  • Assist with collections follow-up under PC direction, on outreach the PC has approved.
  • Track AR aging and prepare the follow-up list for the PC.
  • Assist with post-completion client follow-up.

Working Under PC Direction

  • Take direction from the Project Coordinator supported, and keep them current on what has and has not been done.
  • Apply CELCO's coordination standards consistently across documentation, authorizations, scheduling, and collections support.
  • Surface anything that looks stalled, undocumented, or at risk rather than waiting to be asked.
  • Ask when unsure — an assumption in the paperwork becomes a delay or an unpaid invoice.

Authority

  • Execution of assigned coordination and documentation tasks within PC direction.
  • Flagging missing documentation, signatures, or approvals.
  • Note: authorization decisions, collections strategy, and documentation-standard calls remain with the Project Coordinator.

Key partnerships

Reports To
Project Coordinator Manager
Day-to-Day Direction
Project Coordinators
Works With
Project ManagerAccounting
Success definition

A successful Assistant Project Coordinator reliably takes documentation and coordination load off the Project Coordinators. Job files stay current, paperwork is prepared and filed to standard, and missing signatures and documentation are surfaced early. The PCs are freed to run the division's coordination.
